To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The attitude-behavior relation can be explained by a process model in which self regulatory mechanisms are central.

(1) attitudes are not a sufficient determinant of intentions, (2) intentions are not a necessary determinant of actions, and (3) the relationship between attitudes and intentions is moderated by self regulatory processes.

(1) attitudes, subjective norms, and past behavior predict intentions to engage in health-related behaviors and (2) that the attitude-intention link is mediated by self regulatory processes, which in turn are influenced by emotional reactions to evaluative appraisais.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive and motivational determinants of attitudes, intentions and behavior and the role of affect in attitude formation and change.
the self-regulation of attitudes and intentions and with their role in the initiation and control of social action.
the self regulation of attitudes and behavior, and with the self regulation processes involved in attitude and intention formation and in action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self regulation is an important determinant of attitudes and behavior and is a crucial link in the attitude intention link.
the theory of planned behavior is an excellent theory, but not a sufficient one, and that the theory of reasoned action, as it is currently formulated, is not sufficient either.
self-regulation of attitudes is a function of the interplay between cognitive and affective processes and that the interplay is a function of situational factors and personality characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
attitudes are not sufficient determinatives of intentions and that attitudes do not always lead to behavior.
attitudes and norms are not sufficient to predict intentions and that intentions and norms are not necessary for predicting behavior.
the self regulation of behavior is not just a function of attitudes and intentions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self regulation of attitudes and intentions is an important determinant of behavior.
attitude theory is not complete without a focus on the self regulatory processes that underlie the attitude intention link and the intention behavior link.
attitude-behavior relations depend on the self regulation of attitudes and that the self regulation of emotions is a critical determinant of behavior.
